predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's Spanish Empire shape of 1534 within modern Mexico, without Chiapas (Captaincy General of Guatemala)

successors.name: First Mexican Empire
successors.text: New Spain at its end: Mexico without Chiapas, New Mexico, Texas and the Californias

ledger.x: 1535 (12 October): the Viceroyalty of New Spain is created at Mexico City.
1548: the Audiencia of Guadalajara is set up for Nueva Galicia.
1598 (12 July): Oñate founds the colony of Santa Fe de Nuevo Mexico.
1680: the Pueblo Revolt expels the Spanish from New Mexico.
1692: the Spanish return to New Mexico after twelve years.
1716: Texas becomes a buffer against French Louisiana.
1762 (3 November): the dispute over East Texas ends with the cession of Louisiana.
1776: the Californias join the Commandancy General of the Provincias Internas.
1803: the Louisiana Purchase puts the United States on the Texas border.
1810: the Mexican War of Independence begins.
1819 (22 February): the Adams-Onís Treaty fixes the northern boundary.
1821: the war ends with Mexican independence.
1821: New Spain ends in Mexican independence.

wars.name: Mexican War of Independence
wars.outcome: Independence: 'In 1821, New Spain officially became the independent nation of Mexico'; the viceroyalty was dissolved and the Mexican Empire established.

wars.name: Pueblo Revolt
wars.outcome: The Pueblo peoples drove the Spanish out of New Mexico for twelve years; Spanish rule was restored in 1692.

wars.name: Louisiana Purchase boundary dispute (Texas and the Neutral Ground)
wars.outcome: No war: a Neutral Ground between the Sabine and Arroyo Hondo from 1806; the Adams-Onís Treaty of 22 February 1819 fixed the Sabine boundary.

certainty.note: Colonial frontiers are lines of settlement, mission and presidio, not surveyed borders; the northern and Pacific frontiers of New Spain are approximate throughout.
The boundary with the United States (Sabine, Red River, 100 W, Arkansas, 42 N) is fixed by the Adams-Onís Treaty of 22 February 1819, in force 22 February 1821; every other frontier stays soft.
